purpose: When a whole-study total may be computed from the arms instead of read from the paper. Written as a contract rather than as code branches so that the conditions cannot be relaxed one call site at a time, and so that a run can record which version of them it applied.
doctrine: The model reports what the paper says; this policy decides whether that is enough to permit arithmetic. The model is never permitted to add anything up, to choose which population answers a claim, or to assert a partition the paper does not itself describe.
why_v2: v1 let four wrong totals through. A component could sit in a population set its own quote did not support; the arm census was believed rather than read out of the passage behind it; one arm offered twice with the same count was summed twice; and a timepoint was only ever used to choose between sets, never to refuse the only one. Each is now a condition below.

applies_to.why_narrow: Counts of people partition; almost nothing else does. Summing arm-level means, medians, rates or hazard ratios is wrong even when every component is anchored, so the permission is granted by an explicit list rather than withheld by one.

invariants._note: Not switches. These are always enforced; they are written down so the file describes the behaviour completely, and the loader refuses a policy that claims to disable one.

statuses.derived: every requirement was met and the components were added by deterministic code
statuses.rejected: the paper's own evidence does not establish that the components are complete, mutually exclusive, and one population at one time
statuses.protocol_error: the response was malformed: a non-integer count, an unanchored quote, an arm offered twice, or a census the partition passage does not support
statuses.not_applicable: no arithmetic was attempted, because the paper prints the total itself or the field is not one this policy permits summing

notes: A boolean is not evidence. `complete: true` with no locatable quote is treated exactly as `complete: false`.

A boolean about a list the code cannot see is unfalsifiable, so `complete` alone is never enough: the partition passage must itself say how many groups there are, or name them, and the components in hand must match that exactly — not merely fail to be missing one.

Belonging to a set does not make a count belong to that set's population. Each component's own quote must be shown to carry the set's population phrase, and its timepoint phrase where there is one; otherwise an analysed count can be added to allocated ones by being listed beside them.
One arm offered twice is a protocol error whether or not the two counts agree. Agreeing counts are the more dangerous case, because the sum still looks plausible.
A timepoint the claim declares must be matched even when only one set is on offer. Being the only candidate is not evidence of being the right one.

Populations are matched on BOTH axes. analysed/ITT and analysed/per-protocol are different people; an unspecified analysis set is unknown rather than compatible, and unknown is refused when the review named one.
An explicit total that disagrees with a valid sum is not resolved by preferring either one. Both are reported and the claim is refused.

Where the printed totals contradict each other, no sum may be offered instead. Arithmetic that resolves a paper's self-disagreement is not a reading of the paper; it is a decision about which of its statements to ignore.
